sections.overview: Tubifex tubifex is a freshwater oligochaete annelid that burrows in bottom sediment.
sections.identification: It is usually a slender, reddish worm; the posterior end may wave above the mud.
sections.habitat: It lives in many freshwater sediments, from clean lakes to polluted rivers, and tolerates low oxygen. A Canadian review reports feeding within roughly the upper 10 cm of sediment.
sections.diet: It ingests fine sediment and digests selected bacteria and other organic material.
sections.behavior: The worm keeps its anterior end in the sediment while extending and waving its tail in the water.
sections.reproduction: It reproduces sexually and lays eggs in cocoons; parthenogenesis is also reported in some populations or conditions.
sections.ecology: It can become very abundant in oxygen-poor, organically polluted sediment, but is also recorded in cleaner waters.
sections.conservation: The cited sources describe ecology and taxonomy but provide no conservation assessment for this common freshwater worm.
